{{Short description|Approach to education}}

'''Mathematics for social justice''' is a [[Pedagogy|pedagogical]] approach to [[mathematics education]] that seeks to incorporate lessons from [[critical mathematics pedagogy]] and similar educational philosophies into the teaching of mathematics at schools and colleges. The approach tries to empower students on their way to developing a positive mathematics identity and becoming active, numerically literate citizens who can navigate and participate in society.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Gutstein |first=Eric |date=2003 |title=Teaching and Learning Mathematics for Social Justice in an Urban, Latino School |url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/30034699 |journal=Journal for Research in Mathematics Education |language=en |volume=34 |issue=1 |pages=37–73 |doi=10.2307/30034699|jstor=30034699 |url-access=subscription }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last=Frankenstein |first=Marilyn |date=2006 |title=Reading the World with Math |journal=Rethinking Mathematics: Teaching Social Justice by the Numbers (Eric Gutstein, Ed.)}}</ref> Mathematics for [[social justice]] puts particular emphasis on overcoming social inequalities.<ref>{{Cite book |last=Gutstein |first=Eric |title=Reading And Writing The World With Mathematics: Toward a Pedagogy for Social Justice |publisher=Routledge |year=2006 |isbn=9780415950848}}</ref> Its proponents, for example, [[Bob Moses (activist)|Bob Moses]],<ref>{{Cite book |last=Moses |first=Robert |title=Radical Equations: Civil Rights from Mississippi |publisher=Beacon Press |year=2002 |isbn=9780807031278}}</ref> may understand numerical literacy as a civil right. Many of the founders of the movement, e.g. Eric Gutstein, were initially mathematics teachers,<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Buell |first1=Catherine A. |last2=Shulman |first2=Bonnie |date=2019 |title=An Introduction to Mathematics for Social Justice |journal=PRIMUS |language=en |volume=29 |issue=3–4 |pages=205–209 |doi=10.1080/10511970.2018.1530707 |issn=1051-1970|doi-access=free }}</ref> but the movement has since expanded to include the teaching of mathematics at colleges and universities.<ref>{{Cite book |last1=Karaali |first1=Gizem |title=Mathematics for Social Justice: Resources for the College Classroom |last2=Khadjavi |first2=Lily |publisher=MAA Press: An Imprint of the American Mathematical Society |year=2019 |isbn=978-1-4704-4926-1}}</ref> Their educational approach is influenced by earlier [[critical pedagogy]] advocates such as [[Paulo Freire]] and others.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Stinson |first1=D. |last2=Bidwell |first2=C.R. |last3=Powell |first3=G.C. |date=2012 |title=Critical pedagogy and teaching mathematics for social justice. |url=https://libjournal.uncg.edu/ijcp/article/view/302 |journal=The International Journal of Critical Pedagogy |volume=4 |issue=1 |pages=76–94}}</ref> Mathematics for social justice has been criticised, however, its proponents argue that it both fits into existing teaching frameworks and promotes students' success in mathematics.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Dover |first=Alison George |date=2009 |title=Teaching for Social Justice and K-12 Student Outcomes: A Conceptual Framework and Research Review |url=http://www.tandfonline.com/doi/abs/10.1080/10665680903196339 |journal=Equity & Excellence in Education |language=en |volume=42 |issue=4 |pages=506–524 |doi=10.1080/10665680903196339 |s2cid=145272026 |issn=1066-5684|url-access=subscription }}</ref>

Mathematics for social justice often overlaps with other approaches to mathematics education, the practice and research of mathematics, including [[ethics in mathematics]]<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Buell |first1=Catherine |last2=Piercey |first2=Victor |date=2022 |title=Special Issue on Ethics in Mathematics |url=https://scholarship.claremont.edu/jhm/vol12/iss2/ |journal=Journal of Humanistic Mathematics |volume=12 |issue=2|doi=10.5642/jhummath.KXCU6801 |s2cid=252698507 |doi-access=free }}</ref> and [[ethnomathematics]].<ref>{{Cite journal |last=D’Ambrosio |first=Ubiratan |author-link=Ubiratan D'Ambrosio |date=2007 |title=PEACE, SOCIAL JUSTICE AND ETHNOMATHEMATICS |url=https://citeseerx.ist.psu.edu/document?repid=rep1&type=pdf&doi=c7db5d946a8e92f853c35ea5e0abbe31705c9cc0#page=35 |journal=The Montana Mathematics Enthusiast |volume=1.2007}}</ref> Common to these approaches is that they can be understood as a sociopolitical turn in mathematics.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Gutiérrez |first=Rochelle |date=2013 |title=The Sociopolitical Turn in Mathematics Education |url=https://pubs.nctm.org/view/journals/jrme/44/1/article-p37.xml |journal=Journal for Research in Mathematics Education |volume=44 |issue=1 |pages=37–68 |doi=10.5951/jresematheduc.44.1.0037 |issn=0021-8251|url-access=subscription }}</ref>

== Criticism ==
Pedagogical approaches incorporating issues of social justice into mathematics classrooms have been heavily criticised by some mathematicians and educators.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Fortin |first1=Jacey |title=California Tries to Close the Gap in Math, but Sets Off a Backlash |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2021/11/04/us/california-math-curriculum-guidelines.html |website=[[The New York Times]] |access-date=24 October 2023}}</ref> They argue that mathematics is neutral and that its education and research should be separated from issues of social justice.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Crowell |first=Rachel |title=New Math Research Group Reflects a Schism in the Field |url=https://www.scientificamerican.com/article/new-math-research-group-reflects-a-schism-in-the-field/ |access-date=2023-08-13 |website=Scientific American |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |date=2021-05-24 |title=Opinion {{!}} In California, 2+2=4 May Be Thought Racist |language=en-US |work=Wall Street Journal |url=https://www.wsj.com/articles/in-california-2-2-4-may-be-thought-racist-11621876555 |access-date=2023-08-13 |issn=0099-9660}}</ref> Balancing the requirements of a mathematical education that teaches students mathematical skills and social justice can be difficult.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Bartell |first=Tonya Gau |date=2013 |title=Learning to Teach Mathematics for Social Justice: Negotiating Social Justice and Mathematical Goals |url=https://pubs.nctm.org/view/journals/jrme/44/1/article-p129.xml |journal=Journal for Research in Mathematics Education |volume=44 |issue=1 |pages=129–163 |doi=10.5951/jresematheduc.44.1.0129 |issn=0021-8251|url-access=subscription }}</ref> Some of its opponents use this to argue against mathematics for social justice because it would necessarily come at the expense of teaching mathematical knowledge.<ref>{{Cite magazine |last=Kang |first=Jay Caspian |date=2022-11-15 |title=How Math Became an Object of the Culture Wars |language=en-US |magazine=The New Yorker |url=https://www.newyorker.com/news/our-columnists/how-math-became-an-object-of-the-culture-wars |access-date=2023-08-13 |issn=0028-792X}}</ref>

Eric Gutstein's book [[Rethinking Mathematics]] has been said to calculate controversy<ref>{{Cite web |date=2007-09-30 |title=NEA: April 2006 NEA Today - Up Front |url=http://www.nea.org/neatoday/0604/upfront14.html |access-date=2023-08-13 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070930185520/http://www.nea.org/neatoday/0604/upfront14.html |archive-date=2007-09-30 }}</ref> and to unnecessarily bring partisan politics into mathematics. The criticism is shared with other works in this area.
